Why a crane changes everything

Up and over — never dropped

In a Brooklyn backyard, there's rarely room to fell a tree. The crane turns a dangerous drop into a controlled lift, piece by piece.

1

Rig it

Each section is strapped and balanced before a single cut is made — the crane holds the weight, not the roof below it.

2

Cut it

The climber cuts the rigged section free while the operator keeps constant tension. Nothing falls; everything is held.

3

Lift it out

Sections swing clear of houses, fences, and wires, and land in the street-side loading zone — not in your garden.

4

Chip & clean

Brush is chipped, logs are hauled, the stump is ground on request, and the site is left clean enough to use that day.

24/7 emergency response

        
Tree down? Read this first.

        
Emergency calls run around the clock. While you wait for the callback, three things protect your house and your claim.

      

      

        
1 · Get clear of it
Keep people and pets out of the room or yard under a leaning tree or a roof-loaded limb. A hung-up tree is under tension and can shift without warning.

        
2 · Photograph everything
Shoot the damage before anything moves — roof, fence, car, and the tree itself, from a safe distance. Insurers want the before pictures, and the crew plans better with them.

        
3 · Call or build the summary
Call (917) 201-8614 any hour, or pick “Emergency / storm” and “Leaning / dead / storm-hit” in the estimate builder, attach your photos list, and request the callback. The crew sees the hazard before they roll.

Straight answers

        
Before you book

      

      

        
Is the estimate really free?
Yes. Describe the tree in the builder above and request the callback — the estimate visit and the quote are free, and you're not committed to anything by asking.

        
Why won't you quote a price on this page?
Because tree prices turn on size, access, and what's underneath the canopy — quoting blind helps nobody. The builder captures exactly those details so the free estimate you get is a real one.

        
When does a job need the crane?
When the tree is extra-large, dead and brittle, leaning over a structure, or boxed in so sections can't be lowered by rope. Mark “Over the house,” “No truck access,” or the 75 ft+ size in the builder and the crane plan gets priced into the free estimate.

        
What happens to the wood and brush?
Brush is chipped and hauled, logs are removed, and stump grinding is available on the same visit when you select it. Note in the form if you'd like firewood rounds left behind.

        
Do you work in winter and after storms?
Yes — emergency response is 24/7, and storm work is a core part of the schedule. After a major storm, the summary builder is the fastest way to get your hazard in the queue with photos noted.

        
What areas do you cover?
The company is based in Brooklyn, NY. Add your neighborhood and cross streets in the builder — coverage is confirmed on the callback before anything is booked.
